This year’s olive harvest has been the most violent in recent memory, with settler attacks on Palestinian farmers reaching a new high. But for Masafer Yatta, this is only the latest escalation in a decades-long campaign by the Israeli state to expel Palestinians from their land by any means necessary. Working in coordination with the army and police, nearby settlers wage a ceaseless battle against the Palestinians living in this area. Professor Ilan Pappé describes what has been happening to Masafer Yatta since the 1970’s as “incremental colonization, ethnic cleansing, and oppression,” and to be here is to see it firsthand. But the people of Masafer Yatta have earned a reputation for themselves for their resistance to state and settler terror. They simply refuse to leave, and the Israelis simply won’t stop trying to force them to. The Nakba never ended. We’re just watching its latest act.

North Bergen raised the Palestinian flag outside Town Hall for the 10th year on Friday, Nov. 13, at an event organized by the New Jersey chapter of American Muslims for Palestine. "It's important for us to honor every community, every culture. That's what North Bergen is about. Unity," Mayor Hugo Cabrera said. Cabrera said he hopes for peace and solidarity around the world. "What they're going through right now is horrible, and hopefully the future can get a little brighter for them," Cabrera said. North Bergen resident Bader Risheg thanked Cabrera and the Board of Commissioners for supporting the annual flag raising. "All we're asking for is just the same as everyone else, it's equality," Risheg said. "Hopefully one day, sooner than later, that there'll be a free Palestine and that they'll receive the same dignity and humanity that we want here in America."

A mass funeral was held on 15 November for 70 Palestinians whose bodies and remains were recovered by rescue teams from under the rubble in Gaza. Some of the burial shrouds hold only fragments of the dead, with families having identified their loved ones from pieces of clothing, hair, teeth, and other small remains. The 70 Palestinians had been under the rubble for more than three years after being killed by Israeli bombs. Around 8,000 people are thought to be still under the rubble.
